body.p: , after , , , , , , . The EXPath File Module 4.0 is the optional feature sxml_expath_file_feature() ("expath-file") over a host interface, the file system.

item.p: Public, additive: include/sxml/processor.h gains the file system (sxml_file_system: an operations table with the directory, path and line separators and ten operations, describe, read, write, list, create_directory, remove, move, create_temporary, get_directory and canonicalize, each over request structs) and the configuration field , next to the resolver and the clock. name.h (frozen by ) gains SXML_NAMESPACE_EXPATH_FILE = 14 (http://expath.org/ns/file); SXML_NAMESPACE_WELL_KNOWN_COUNT is 15.

Opt-in twice (): the host names the feature and gives a file system. sxml_all_optional_features() leaves the feature out, so naming every feature never grants file access. Without the feature the functions are absent (XPST0017); with it and the null file system, every function that needs files raises file:io-error.

Rows: 37 functions in src/function_library_file.c, the definition's library_functions (). Paths are made absolute against CURRENT and normalized lexically in the library, so the host sees only absolute paths; directory paths end with the separator. Text goes through src/text_decoding.c (decoding moved there by ; the encoder of bin:encode-string moves there too). Errors are in the file namespace, filled into the error record (static text). file:move onto an existing directory moves into it, overwriting a file of the same name, as file:copy does.
No recursion (): copy, delete, size and list of a directory walk it with a work list; file:descendants is a resumable body that asks the evaluator to call its filter and recurse predicates.
System property: supports-file-library is a KNOWN_FUNCTION row () for file:exists#1.

CLI: apps/sxml/platform_file_system.c implements the interface over POSIX (realpath is a copy under WASI). sxml xpath and sxml xquery name the feature and pass the file system only with --allow-file-access; they bind the prefixes bin and file always. Windows is not implemented: initialization reports SXML_STATUS_UNSUPPORTED_FEATURE, and the CLI runs without files.

QT4 driver: names the feature for a test case with a sandpit or the dependency feature expath-file. A sandpit is copied through the host file system to a fresh temporary root (root/sandpit is CURRENT, root/temp is TEMPORARY), served by a wrapping file system, and deleted after the case. expath-file is no longer a non-goal feature, nor expath-* a non-goal set, and sandpits are no longer unsupported.

Counts (release driver): expath-file not run to 270 of 270 (XQ40) and 267 of 267 (XP40, 3 not run, XQuery-only); fn-system-properties 23 to 23 (supports-file-library passes; the -false case is not run).

Size: about 66 KB of native code (x86-64, release), above the 20–30 KB estimate, none of it in sxml.wasm or sxml-full.wasm, which do not name the feature. The interface and the encoder move cost the modules +164 bytes (sxml.wasm 2,109,988 to 2,110,152 stripped at 531c5b6 and 10ca66e; sxml-full.wasm 2,214,413 to 2,214,593). The core was over its 2,100,000 bytes before this packet; the full module's 3,553,063 at 1e91f97 is fn:transform's ().
